<issue identifier="MM-487">
<title>Notify: expose the send worker's queue depth as a metric</title>
<description>
Follow-up from review on <pull-request id="e7f32e23-c8ed-4199-932e-367026ce4cec" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/custos-sender-notification-config-sender-keys-registration-routes-49f1f8604731">malpercio-dev/ezpds#467</pull-request> (<issue id="66b34b92-3d28-4317-ab71-155977c248e9" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-418/notify-49-custos-sender-config-sender-keys-registration-routes-relay">MM-418</issue>).

The notification send worker (`crates/pds/src/notify_relay_client.rs`) drains an **unbounded** `tokio::sync::mpsc` with a single sequential task. That is the right trade-off for a best-effort, device-count-scaled feature — the queue must never block a request path, and a missed push is a missed banner rather than lost data.

But during a prolonged relay outage (a maintenance window, a misconfigured node id), the queue grows without bound in the interim, and today that is only inferable from `warn!` log volume.

## Scope

Expose the current queue depth as an OTel gauge, following the existing pattern in `crates/pds/src/metrics.rs`:

* add the instrument + its name constant to `metrics::names`
* record depth from the worker (send side increments, `recv` decrements — or sample `len()` if the channel type allows)
* add the row to the metrics table in `crates/pds/AGENTS.md` (that table mirrors `metrics::names` and they change together)
* consider surfacing it in `GET /v1/admin/health` alongside the sweep entries, so the Brass Console can show it

## Why not in the original PR

Out of scope for the sender phase, and it touches the metrics module, its name constants, and the operator docs table — a self-contained change that reviews better on its own.

## Open question

Whether an unbounded queue should stay unbounded once this is observable, or gain a cap that drops oldest-first. Dropping is consistent with the feature's best-effort posture; the metric is the prerequisite for deciding with evidence either way.
</description>

<title>E2E-encrypted notification relay for self-hosted Custos (APNs)</title>
<description>
Implement the notification relay designed in [docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](<https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/blob/main/docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md>) (design PR <pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, **merged** — the doc on `main` is the source of truth and incorporates the review hardening: claim-code enrollment authorization for the official relay, versioned sender keys with re-pin/revocation semantics, explicit v1 replay acceptance, unverified-notice rendering for unauthenticated payloads, per-handle APNs topics, serialized-request padding budget, and the post-reboot keychain window).

## Problem

Self-hosted Custos instances need to deliver push notifications to the official iOS apps (Obsign, admin-companion). APNs auth keys are bundle-ID-bound, so self-hosters cannot push directly — a relay is structurally required. The design makes that relay a **blind courier**: trusted for availability only.

## Architecture (see design doc for full detail)

* **Confidentiality:** payloads HPKE-sealed (RFC 9180, DHKEM-P256 + AES-GCM) to a per-device notification key; decrypted on-device by a Notification Service Extension (`mutable-content: 1`). Neither the relay nor Apple sees plaintext.
* **Integrity:** HPKE Auth mode with pinned, versioned per-instance sender keys — the relay cannot forge authenticated content (it can generate detectable junk pushes and replay; v1 accepts duplicates as benign).
* **Metadata minimization:** opaque push handles bound to the instance's iroh node id (no DIDs/handles/raw tokens at the relay), fixed-size padding budgeted against the serialized APNs request, optional content-free ping mode.
* **Transport:** Custos ↔ relay over iroh, new `ezpds/notify/0` ALPN, reusing the persisted node identity (`iroh_identity`) and `iroh_tunnel.rs` patterns; back-channel carries APNs `410 Unregistered` pruning feedback.
* **Sovereignty:** relay is an open-source workspace crate (`crates/notify-relay/`); any instance points at any relay via `[notifications] relay = "<node id>"`. Official relay requires a claim-code enrollment grant; open enrollment is a config option for self-run relays. Caveat: official bundle IDs require the official relay's APNs key.

## Suggested phasing

1. **Relay crate + Custos sender** — `crates/notify-relay/` (claim-code enrollment grants, handle store with per-handle APNs topic, APNs HTTP/2 client, per-node rate limits, serialized-request size validation with 4 KB boundary test) + `[notifications]` config, device notification-key registration route, versioned sender-key set, sealed-send on first trigger (agent claim pending). Loopback iroh e2e tests with mock APNs.
2. **Wallet NSE** — per-device keypair + shared keychain access group, registration in onboarding, decrypt-and-render extension, unverified-notice fallback + in-app diagnostics.
3. **Admin-companion adoption + operator docs** — ops alert triggers, self-relay runbook, metadata-minimizing ping mode.

## Open questions (from the design doc)

* Enrollment grant distribution for the official relay (ceremony mirrors admin-device pairing)
* Replay hardening beyond v1's accept-duplicates posture (per-device counter + durable replay window)
* Delivery receipts over the iroh back-channel (out of scope v1)
* Android/FCM later (envelope is provider-agnostic)

Not yet scheduled into a wave; split into per-phase issues when picked up.
</description>
</parent-issue>

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

3	//! OTel metrics meter + Prometheus registry behind `GET /metrics`.
4	//!
5	//! One [`Metrics`] value lives in `AppState` for the process lifetime and exposes a typed
6	//! handle per instrument — call sites record measurements through these fields rather than
7	//! looking instruments up by name. The meter rides the same `opentelemetry` 0.32 line as the
8	//! trace pipeline in `telemetry.rs`; the `opentelemetry-prometheus` bridge collects into a
9	//! `prometheus::Registry` that [`Metrics::render`] encodes as text exposition format.
10	//!
11	//! When `[telemetry] metrics_enabled = false`, [`Metrics::disabled`] builds the same typed
12	//! handles against a reader-less meter provider: measurements are dropped at the SDK
13	//! boundary, no registry exists, and `app()` never registers the route — so call sites stay
14	//! unconditional while the endpoint 404s.
15	//!
16	//! Instrument names and label keys live in [`names`] — the single source of truth the
17	//! documentation table in `crates/pds/AGENTS.md` mirrors. Counters are named **without**
18	//! the `_total` suffix: the Prometheus exporter appends it per the OpenTelemetry
19	//! Prometheus-compatibility spec (the unit test below pins the rendered names so drift or
20	//! a double suffix fails fast).
21

23	use axum::extract::{MatchedPath, Request, State};

236	            admin_nonce_sweep_swept: meter.u64_counter(names::ADMIN_NONCE_SWEEP_SWEPT).build(),
237	            admin_nonce_sweep_last_run_timestamp: meter
238	                .f64_gauge(names::ADMIN_NONCE_SWEEP_LAST_RUN_TIMESTAMP)

256	    /// Encode the current registry contents as Prometheus text exposition format.
257	    /// Returns `None` when metrics are disabled (the route is not registered in that
258	    /// case, so in practice this is only `None` for direct callers in tests).
259	    pub fn render(&self) -> Option<anyhow::Result<String>> {
260	        let registry = self.registry.as_ref()?;
261	        let mut buf = Vec::new();
262	        let result = TextEncoder::new()
263	            .encode(&registry.gather(), &mut buf)
264	            .context("failed to encode metrics")
265	            .and_then(|()| String::from_utf8(buf).context("metrics output was not UTF-8"));
266	        Some(result)
267	    }
268	}

270	/// Record one measurement with a single label — the dominant call shape.
271	pub fn label(key: &'static str, value: impl Into<opentelemetry::Value>) -> KeyValue {
272	    KeyValue::new(key, value.into())
273	}
274	
275	/// Current unix time in seconds, for the `*_last_run_timestamp` gauges.
276	pub fn unix_now() -> f64 {
277	    chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() as f64
278	}

280	/// RAII guard for the `firehose_subscribers` gauge: `+1` on construction, `−1` on drop.
281	///
282	/// The WebSocket handler holds one for the life of the connection, so every exit path —
283	/// clean close, lagged disconnect, error frame, task abort — decrements exactly once and
284	/// the gauge cannot drift from the true connection count.
285	pub struct SubscriberGuard(std::sync::Arc<Metrics>);
286	
287	impl SubscriberGuard {
288	    pub fn connect(metrics: std::sync::Arc<Metrics>) -> Self {
289	        metrics.firehose_subscribers.add(1, &[]);
290	        Self(metrics)
291	    }
292	}

294	impl Drop for SubscriberGuard {
295	    fn drop(&mut self) {
296	        self.0.firehose_subscribers.add(-1, &[]);
297	    }
298	}

300	/// Count every routed request into `http_requests_total` by route template + status class.
301	///
302	/// The route label comes from axum's [`MatchedPath`] — the template (`/xrpc/{method}`),
303	/// never the raw URI — so series cardinality is bounded by the route table. Requests that
304	/// match no route fall into a single `unmatched` series. Layered outside the rate limiter
305	/// (so 429s are counted) and inside CORS (so short-circuited preflights are not).
306	pub async fn http_metrics_middleware(
307	    State(state): State<AppState>,
308	    req: Request,
309	    next: Next,
310	) -> Response {
311	    let route = req
312	        .extensions()
313	        .get::<MatchedPath>()
314	        .map(|p| p.as_str().to_owned())
315	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "unmatched".to_owned());
316	    let response = next.run(req).await;
317	    state.metrics.http_requests.add(
318	        1,
319	        &[
320	            label(names::LABEL_ROUTE, route),
321	            label(
322	                names::LABEL_STATUS_CLASS,
323	                status_class(response.status().as_u16()),
324	            ),
325	        ],
326	    );
327	    response
328	}

330	/// Collapse an HTTP status code into its class label value (`2xx`, `4xx`, …).
331	pub fn status_class(status: u16) -> &'static str {
332	    match status / 100 {
333	        1 => "1xx",
334	        2 => "2xx",
335	        3 => "3xx",
336	        4 => "4xx",
337	        5 => "5xx",
338	        _ => "other",
339	    }
340	}

353	        metrics.http_requests.add(

366	            .blob_gc_last_run_timestamp

375	        );

379	        );

382	            "missing firehose_subscribers gauge in:\n{rendered}"
383	        );

386	            "missing firehose_events_total in:\n{rendered}"
387	        );

# PDS Crate (Custos)

Last verified: 2026-07-27

## Purpose

The PDS is the axum-based web server. It is the sole Imperative Shell in the workspace —
the only crate that touches SQLite, handles HTTP, or manages process-level state. All other
crates (`crypto`, `repo-engine`, `common`) are pure Functional Cores that the PDS calls.

## Module Map

```
src/
  main.rs          — startup: open pool, run migrations, bind server
  telemetry.rs     — OTel tracing-subscriber init (`init_subscriber`) + shutdown-flushing `OtelGuard`; wired by main.rs at startup, dropped after graceful shutdown. `[telemetry] log_format = "json"` switches the stdout fmt layer to one-JSON-object-per-line
  metrics.rs       — OTel meter + Prometheus registry behind `GET /metrics` (see "Metrics" section below): typed `Metrics` handle in AppState, instrument/label name constants (`metrics::names`), the `http_requests_total` middleware, and the `SubscriberGuard` RAII gauge
  app.rs           — router construction (route table + shared middleware layers); re-exports `AppState`/`FailedLoginStore` (and, under `#[cfg(test)]`, `test_state`/`test_state_with_plc_url`) from `state.rs` so the ~120 existing `crate::app::AppState` imports across the crate stay unchanged
  state.rs         — `AppState` definition + `FailedLoginStore`, plus the `#[cfg(test)]` `test_state`/`test_state_with_plc_url` constructors
  xrpc_dispatch.rs — the catch-all XRPC proxy dispatcher (`xrpc_handler`, registered by `app.rs` at `/xrpc/{method}`): resolves `app.bsky.*`/`chat.bsky.*`/`com.atproto.moderation.*` to an upstream (configured default or an `atproto-proxy`-header target), enforces the read-after-write munge branch, and records `proxy_requests_total`
  firehose/        — persistent subscribeRepos event pipeline (durable sequencer + broadcast fan-out)
  firehose_gc.rs   — periodic `repo_seq` retention sweep (age/count pruning below the live frontier)
  blob_store.rs    — blob storage backend: filesystem I/O, CID computation, MIME-type detection; blobs live at `{data_dir}/blobs/{cid[0:2]}/{cid}`
  blob_gc.rs       — periodic blob GC over per-account ownership rows (`blob_owners`, V039): reconciles each account's MST-referenced blobs into its ownership rows (permanent vs released-with-grace, adopting referenced-but-unowned stored CIDs), then sweeps expired unreferenced rows — the shared physical row + file are deleted only when the last owner is gone. The sweep **fails closed on a failed reconcile**: an account whose repo walk errored this pass is excluded from it by DID, because its `temp_until` pins were never cleared and the global sweep cannot otherwise tell "references nothing" from "references unknown". Such an account leaks disk until the fault is fixed, and is reported via `blob_gc_errors_total` + the sweep snapshot's `errors`
  blob_mirror/     — off-volume blob replication to an S3-compatible bucket (`[blob_mirror]` / `EZPDS_BLOB_MIRROR_*`, the Litestream analogue for blob files, which Litestream never covers): `mod.rs` is the periodic sweep (template: blob_gc.rs — upload verified-missing keys, propagate row deletions on a harmless lag, with a tripwire refusing delete propagation when the `blobs` table is empty against a non-empty bucket) plus `restore_missing_blobs`, run by main.rs *before the listener binds* so a Litestream-restored DB is reconciled with the blob directory before anything is served; `s3.rs` is a minimal hand-rolled SigV4 client (put/get/delete/ListObjectsV2, signing pinned against the AWS documentation's worked examples). Both mirror directions re-hash bytes against their CID (`blob_store::compute_cid`) before trusting them: a corrupt local file never becomes the recovery copy, and a corrupt bucket copy is never materialised at a valid CID path. `BlobMirror::fetch_verified` (fetch + verify one CID) is the shared entry point `blob_scrub.rs`'s auto-heal reuses. `test_support.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`) holds the shared fake-S3 test double + `BlobMirror` builder both this module's and `blob_scrub.rs`'s tests use
  blob_scrub.rs    — periodic blob-integrity scrub sweep (`[blob_scrub]` / `EZPDS_BLOB_SCRUB_*`, template: blob_gc.rs, same failed-pass-leaves-timestamp-stale posture): re-hashes every stored blob's file against its `blobs` row (hash + size) and walks the blob directory for both orphan directions nothing else scans for — a row whose file is missing (the migration-blocking fault) and a file no row owns (a leak `blob_gc` never sees, since it only ever works from DB rows outward). When `[blob_mirror]` is configured and `auto_heal` is on, a bad/missing file is repaired from the bucket's verified copy (`BlobMirror::fetch_verified`, written back through `blob_store::store_blob`'s durable temp-file+fsync+rename path so a healed file is exactly as crash-durable as a fresh upload); otherwise the problem is only ever flagged, converting silent rot into an operator signal
  crawler.rs       — outbound requestCrawl notifier (rate-limited, retrying, fire-and-forget)
  relay_status.rs  — inbound `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` client: asks the upstream relay what it knows about this PDS (its cursor into our seq-space, indexed-account count, lifecycle status), total/never-fatal (every failure is a `RelayReport` variant). Backs `GET /v1/admin/relay-status`
  email.rs         — pluggable outbound email sender (`Arc<dyn EmailSender>` in AppState): `LogEmailSender` (default; logs instead of sending — keeps tests/fresh installs offline) + `SmtpEmailSender` (real delivery via `lettre`, rustls) + `HttpEmailSender` (real delivery via Mailtrap's transactional HTTPS Send API over `reqwest`, `provider = "mailtrap"`; needs only outbound HTTPS, so it works where outbound SMTP ports are blocked — e.g. Railway's non-Pro plans). Backs the password-reset / email-confirmation / email-update / PLC-op / account-delete token deliveries. Configured by `[email]` in `pds.toml` / `EZPDS_EMAIL_*` (Mailtrap: `EZPDS_EMAIL_HTTP_TOKEN`, optional `EZPDS_EMAIL_HTTP_API_URL` / `EZPDS_EMAIL_HTTP_TIMEOUT_SECS`)
  rate_limit.rs    — request rate-limiting middleware + shared limiter state (global IP, per-endpoint IP, per-account write points)
  iroh_tunnel.rs   — Iroh QUIC endpoint: NAT-traversing device↔pds tunnel (opt-in)
  notify_relay_client.rs — the pds's first *outbound* iroh leg: dials the configured notification relay (`ezpds/notify/0`) from the same `IrohState` endpoint `iroh_tunnel.rs` accepts on, so the instance presents one node identity — which is exactly the identity the relay authorizes (`connection.remote_id()`; no credential travels in a message). One JSON request per bidi stream, lazily-dialed cached connection with a one-shot re-dial retry (the expected failure is a *stale* connection after a relay restart), and enroll-on-`notEnrolled` rather than a startup step, so a relay that is restarted or reached first mid-run heals by itself. Also owns the fire-and-forget send worker: triggers enqueue `NotifyJob`s onto an unbounded in-process mpsc and return immediately, because a trigger that blocks on a push relay has traded a missed banner for a broken request. In-memory only, deliberately — a missed push is a missed *banner*, not lost data (the app reconciles from Custos), so durable queuing would add a table, a sweep, and a retry policy to protect something already recoverable. The worker writes back relay handles and prunes a registration the relay reports `unregistered` (APNs 410)
  notifications.rs — the sending side: `notify_device(state, did, payload)` / `notify_admin_devices` load the registrations, load the active sender key once per fan-out, then **pad and seal once per device** (HPKE seals to a single recipient; reusing an encapsulated key across devices would be a weaker protocol) and enqueue. Padding is computed against the *serialized APNs body* — the only length an observer measures — via the shared `notify_relay::protocol::apns_envelope`, so the sender's arithmetic and the relay's serialization cannot disagree. A payload too large for the top bucket is **dropped**, not sent unpadded or truncated: sending it would leak the exact length padding exists to hide. Sender keys are generated lazily (first send, or first `sender-keys` fetch — an app must be able to pin a key before the first notification arrives). Nothing here is fallible from a caller's perspective; every path ends in an enqueue or a log line. Inert when `[notifications] relay` is unset (`AppState.notify_sender` is `None`), down to never minting key material
  record_write.rs  — shared repo write flow + firehose commit emission + post-commit block GC (reuses the firehose diff's `reachable(new)` set as the GC keep-set, so a commit walks repo reachability once, not again per write — see `gc_repo_blocks`)
  repo_rev.rs      — shared `read_repo_rev` (open a repo at its head, return the commit `rev`, `None` on unreadable/parse failure), homed beside `record_write.rs` so the public sync endpoints (`listRepos`/`getLatestCommit`/`getRepoStatus`) share it without a route-to-route import
  time.rs          — shared epoch/RFC-3339 time helpers (`unix_now` → `Result<u64, ApiError>`, `unix_now_secs` → `i64` clamped, `now_rfc3339`, `to_rfc3339_utc`), previously copy-pasted across routes/guards/firehose; each variant's return type + pre-epoch handling is deliberate — pick by call-site contract
  account_delete.rs— shared permanent account-deletion transaction (all child tables in FK order — no account-keyed FK cascades exist — plus on-disk reclamation of blob files no other account owns and an `#account` deleted frame), used by deleteAccount and the reaper. Purging a parent cascade-schedules its sovereign children onto the same deactivate → `delete_after` → reaper pipeline (their registration/provisioning rows go with the parent, ADR-0023); a schema-walking test (`purge_covers_every_account_foreign_key_in_the_schema`) fails the build if a migration adds an account-keyed FK the purge doesn't reach
  account_reaper.rs— periodic sweep that permanently deletes deactivated accounts past their `deleteAfter` (template: firehose_gc.rs)
  agent_claim_sweep.rs— periodic sweep flipping lapsed pending agent claim attempts to `expired` and recording a `claim_expired` audit event per attempt, in one transaction (template: account_reaper.rs; interval: `[agent_auth] claim_sweep_interval_secs` / `EZPDS_AGENT_CLAIM_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS`)
  labeler_watch.rs — periodic labeler watcher (template: account_reaper.rs, but its first pass runs immediately at boot): polls each `[labeler] watched` labeler's `com.atproto.label.queryLabels` for the hosted DIDs (endpoint resolved from the labeler DID doc's `#atproto_labeler` service entry via `identity::proxy::resolve_atproto_proxy_target`, fetched on the SSRF-hardened client; `uriPatterns` batched at 20 — Ozone silently returns nothing past that) and reconciles `account_labels` (V051) to the labels currently in force. Interval: `[labeler] poll_interval_secs` / `EZPDS_LABELER_*`; spawned only when the watched list is non-empty (startup clears the table otherwise — flagged state never outlives its config)
  label_state.rs   — Functional Core for the watcher: reduce raw label events to the in-force set (`cts` order, `neg` retractions, `exp` expiry, per-labeler watchlist, account-level `did:` subjects only) and diff it against the persisted rows
  admin_nonce_sweep.rs— periodic sweep deleting stale `admin_nonces` rows via `db::admin_devices::sweep_stale_nonces` (template: account_reaper.rs; pure storage reclamation — the `(device_id, nonce)` primary key enforces replay rejection, and config validation keeps `nonce_max_age_secs` above the request's full `2 * common::ADMIN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span so a swept row can never still be within it; interval: `[admin_devices] nonce_sweep_interval_secs` / `EZPDS_ADMIN_DEVICES_NONCE_SWEEP_INTERVAL_SECS`, retention: `nonce_max_age_secs` / `EZPDS_ADMIN_DEVICES_NONCE_MAX_AGE_SECS`)
  sovereign_session_nonce_sweep.rs— hourly sweep deleting `sovereign_session_nonces` rows older than one hour; pure storage reclamation, with a compile-time assertion that retention exceeds the signed request's full `2 * common::SOVEREIGN_TIMESTAMP_WINDOW_SECS` replay-acceptance span
  sweep_status.rs  — readable last-run state per periodic sweep (`AppState.sweeps`): each sweep records `{completed_at, swept}` beside its write-only OTel gauge writes so `GET /v1/admin/health` can report it as JSON; shares the sweeps' failure posture (a failed pass records nothing — staleness is the alarm)
  transfer.rs      — shared planned device-transfer accept/complete/cancel workflows composing multi-table transactions; `db/transfers.rs` owns the SQL, this module owns the cross-table ordering (cancel is the operator interruption: flip to terminal `cancelled`, tombstone the accepted device credential, append a `transfer.cancelled` audit event — existing account sessions deliberately untouched)
  identity/        — everything "who is this handle/DID": resolution chain, handle validation, and did:plc genesis/rotation-op machinery (see below)
  session_issuer.rs— shared legacy access+refresh JWT issuance transaction; explicit full-access vs app-password authority, atomically inserts sessions + initial refresh_tokens, and re-checks app-password existence inside the transaction
  capabilities.rs  — the `CAPABILITIES` table: every capability Custos advertises under `describeServer`'s `custos` extension, each with its wire name, the config that gates it, a one-line summary, and the predicate reading the live `Config`. Pure. The single source of truth for three consumers — `routes/describe_server.rs` (what is advertised), the generated operator reference page (`just docs-generate`), and the documentation-drift gate (`just capability-docs-check`, which fails until `sites/docs/.../operator/capabilities.md` names each capability and its controls). Also owns `IDENTIFYING_VERSION` (`custos vX.Y.Z`, served by `routes/health.rs`). **A capability's `enabled` predicate must be the same condition its routes enforce** — advertising something a caller cannot actually use is a lie the client has no way to detect
  code_gen.rs      — random claim-code generation (pure), shared by claim-code + account-creation routes
  uniqueness.rs    — email/handle pre-flight uniqueness DB checks, shared by the account-creation routes
  platform.rs      — device `Platform` enum, shared by the device-registration routes
  request_host.rs  — `request_host` (Functional Core): resolve the client-addressed host (`X-Forwarded-Host` → `Host` → `:authority`) for the Host-keyed public routes (`.well-known/atproto-did`, `.well-known/did.json`), then strip an explicit default port (`:443`/`:80`, both treated as default since TLS terminates at the proxy) so `Host: example.com:443` keys the same did:web DID / handle as the bare host — a non-default port stays (`did:web:host%3A8080` is a distinct DID); lives outside `routes/` so both handlers share it without a route-to-route import
  lexicon/         — vendored `com.atproto.*` lexicon documents (`crates/pds/lexicons/`, pinned upstream — see its README) compiled into a registry, plus the reference-parity XRPC **input validation layer**: `LexiconInput<T>` (mod `extractor.rs`, Imperative Shell) replaces bare `axum::Json<T>` on every natively-handled JSON procedure, running presence → Content-Type → JSON parse → lexicon-schema checks with `@atproto/xrpc-server`/`@atproto/lexicon`'s byte-identical 400 `InvalidRequest` messages (`Input must have the property "x"`, `Input/handle must be a valid handle`, …) before serde sees the body; `validate_procedure_body` is the same pipeline as a plain call for handlers that also need the raw bytes (admin-signed `updateSubjectStatus`). Schema parsing (`schema.rs`) is strict — unknown keys/def types/string formats and dangling refs fail the registry tests — so re-vendoring can't silently skip a constraint and drift laxer than the reference. String formats dispatch to the fixture-tested validators (`repo_engine::{datetime,at_uri,records}`, `identity::{did,handle}`). The registry also holds the vendored **`app.bsky.*` record lexicons** (posts/likes/reposts/follows/blocks/lists/profiles + the `object`/`string`/`token` defs their record bodies reach; the AppView view/output defs those documents also declare are never validation roots, so they stay un-vendored) and exposes `validate_record` — `assertValidRecord`-parity record validation the repo-write routes (`record_write::write_record`, `apply_writes`) run: reject an invalid record of a known collection by default, honor the `validate` flag (`true` requires validity, `false` skips), enforce `$type == collection` and the record-key discipline (`tid`/`literal:self`/…), and report per-write `validationStatus` (`valid`/`unknown`); unknown collections stay writable and report `unknown`. A companion **query-parameter validation layer** closes the same drift class for GET query strings: `LexiconParams<T>` (mod `params.rs`, Imperative Shell) replaces bare `axum::Query<T>` (and, for `sync.getBlocks`'s repeated `cids=` keys, a hand-rolled `RawQuery` parse) on every natively-handled query, coercing raw (always-string) query values to typed JSON per property (`@atproto/xrpc-server`'s `decodeQueryParams` semantics — an empty value decodes to absent, an unparseable integer falls back to `0` rather than erroring, a boolean is `true` only for the literal string `"true"`, an array is repeated keys) before running the same object-validator required/format/bounds/enum checks an input body uses, yielding the reference's byte-identical `Params must have the property "x"` / `Params/limit can not be greater than 100` messages; `validate_procedure_params`/`validate_params_map` are the same pipeline for a handler needing to adjust the raw query first (`get_record.rs`'s legacy `did=` alias for the lexicon's `repo` parameter). The registry parses `type: "query"` defs (and a `type: "procedure"`'s optional `parameters`) into the same `LexObject` shape a body's properties use, restricted to string/integer/boolean and arrays of them — schema.rs's loud-failure guard rejects anything else (object/ref/union/…) in a params object. A **response-output layer** closes the same drift class for what Custos *serves*: every natively-handled query/procedure's JSON `output` schema is parsed (the shared `schema::parse_xrpc_body` for `input`/`output` alike) and registered by NSID, and `check_refs` walks the output closure at build time — which is what pulls the output-only `defs` documents (`com.atproto.repo.defs#commitMeta`, `com.atproto.identity.defs#identityInfo`) into the vendored set, so a document whose output refs something un-vendored fails `registry_builds` rather than 500ing at serve time. `validate_output(nsid, body)` (rooted at `Output`, `assertValidXrpcOutput` parity) is the drift *detector*. In test builds, `output.rs` wraps the real Axum router and buffers every successful natively-handled response with a registered JSON schema after the handler has serialized its DTO; a missing/renamed field panics the route test, while production and non-JSON streams remain untouched. The malformed-output registry fixtures remain as focused invalid-case coverage
  rewrap.rs        — offline master-key (KEK) re-wrap behind the `pds rewrap-master-key` subcommand: one transaction decrypts every KEK-wrapped secret (inventory in `db/kek.rs`, including `accounts.recovery_share` and the `recovery_escrow` share envelopes — plaintext lengths vary, so the sweep uses the generic-length `crypto::{encrypt,decrypt}_secret_bytes` pair) with the old master key and re-encrypts under the new one; any old-key decrypt failure aborts with no writes (a blob already under the NEW key is diagnosed as a completed prior rotation); bumps the `kek_generation` marker in `server_metadata` in the same transaction. Keys arrive via EZPDS_REWRAP_{OLD,NEW}_MASTER_KEY env vars only (never argv). Server must be stopped (single-connection pool). See docs/deploy.md "Rotating the Master Key"
  recovery_share.rs— encodes the KEK boundary for PDS-held Shamir Share 2: base32↔32-byte conversion, authenticated wrap/unwrap, and the idempotent startup data migration that transactionally replaces legacy 52-character plaintext rows before the server accepts requests
  no_input.rs      — `NoInputBody`: shared axum `FromRequest` extractor guarding XRPC procedures whose lexicon defines no `input`. Rejects any non-empty request body with a 400 `InvalidRequest` ("A request body was provided when none was expected"), byte-for-byte the reference PDS message. Extract it *last* (it consumes the body). Lives outside `routes/` (like `request_host.rs`) so every no-input handler shares one guard — `activateAccount`, `refreshSession`, `deleteSession`, `requestAccountDelete`, `requestEmailConfirmation`, `requestEmailUpdate`, `requestPlcOperationSignature` — instead of the strictness drifting route to route; Custos leniency here was the wallet's blind spot against bsky.social
  read_after_write/— buffered AppView response munge path for read-after-write: merges requester's unindexed records, rev-faithful selection via atproto-repo-rev, fallback ladder, Atproto-Upstream-Lag header
  auth/            — authentication primitives + route guards (HTTP-aware, no DB schema ownership)
  db/              — SQL query functions + migration runner (no business logic)
  routes/          — HTTP handlers, one file per endpoint
```

### `firehose/`

The **persistent** event pipeline behind `com.atproto.sync.subscribeRepos`, split into three
cohesive layers so the subtle invariant-heavy staging code is reviewable in isolation. `mod.rs`
re-exports every submodule's public types (`Firehose`, `FirehoseEvent`, `CommitInput`, `Subscription`,
etc.) at `crate::firehose::*`, so the 19 consumer files address them exactly as before the split.

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | `Firehose` (the durable sequencer + broadcast fan-out), the bare `emit_commit`/`emit_account`/`emit_identity`/`emit_sync` primitives, and the atomic staged-transaction path (`lock_emit`/`EmitGuard`/`PendingCommit`/`PendingAccount`/`PendingWithSync`) — the emit-lock/staging invariants documented below |
| `events.rs` | The wire-facing event model (`RepoOp`, `CommitEvent`, `AccountEvent`, `IdentityEvent`, `SyncEvent`, `FirehoseEvent`), their DAG-CBOR stored-payload encoding, `decode_stored_event` (reconstructs an event from a persisted `repo_seq` row for replay), and the pre-persist wire-CID/CAR-size validation. Pure data + (de)serialization, no `Firehose` state |
| `replay.rs` | Cursor replay over the durable log: `Subscription`/`SubscribeOutcome` (the subscribe handshake) and `ReplayReader` (paged `(cursor, upper]` replay with the best-effort-vs-fail-closed pruning logic) |

The module holds a durable
monotonic sequencer (backed by the `repo_seq` table, V028) and a Tokio `broadcast` channel;
`AppState.firehose: Arc<Firehose>` is shared by every handler. Each repo commit calls
`record_write::commit_repo_write`, which builds the commit's block diff
(`repo_engine::collect_commit_diff` — one walk of the new root, yielding both the `added` diff
blocks and the `new_reachable` keep-set — + `build_car_from_cids`, run *before* post-commit GC) and
publishes a sequenced `CommitEvent` carrying the DID, rev, `since`, `prevData` (the previous
commit's MST root CID — Sync v1.1's inductive-validation anchor, captured before the write mutates
the repo; `None` for genesis), per-record `RepoOp`s (action + collection/rkey + cid + prev + value;
`prev` is the previous record CID for an update/delete — Sync v1.1's per-op inductive-validation
anchor — `None` for a create), and
the CARv1 diff blocks. The `#commit` wire frame emits the deprecated `blobs` list empty. Backpressure is by design: the bounded
channel never blocks producers — a slow subscriber observes `Lagged` and is expected to disconnect.
All three write paths (`create_record`/`put_record` via `record_write`, `delete_record`,
`apply_writes`) emit exactly one event per commit. (Those same write paths reject a deactivated
account with 403 before committing.) `create_did.rs`'s `promote_account` stages the same kind of
`#commit` event for a new account's *genesis* repo, atomically with the `accounts`/`did_documents`/
`sessions` inserts, so a fresh host self-announces to the relay instead of staying invisible until
its first record write; chained after that genesis `#commit` in the same transaction is a Sync v1.1
`#sync` state assertion (via `PendingCommit::stage_sync`, carrying a single-root CAR of just the
signed commit block), so a relay can anchor to this fresh host's head. It then emits a best-effort
`#account` (active) frame and calls `crawlers.notify()` once that transaction has committed.
A `#sync` frame (`SyncEvent`: DID, rev, and a ≤10 KB commit-block CAR) is the Sync v1.1 head
assertion relays use to auto-repair drift; it is emitted on account genesis (above) and on
`activateAccount` (chained after the `#account` via `PendingAccount::stage_sync` when the account
has a repo — the commit-block CAR is built *before* the transaction, since the single-connection
pool can't serve a block read while the tx holds the connection). `importRepo` (shipped,
`routes/import_repo.rs`) deliberately does *not* emit one — a migrated repo's head assertion rides
on the `activateAccount` that follows it in the migration sequence. Account-status changes emit a separate
`#account` frame instead of a `#commit`: `activate_account.rs`/`deactivate_account.rs` stage one
via `Firehose::stage_account` (active=false/`deactivated` or active=true) **only on a real status
transition** — a redundant no-op activate/deactivate returns 200 and emits nothing.
`update_subject_status.rs` (`com.atproto.admin.updateSubjectStatus`) stages the same kind of frame
for an admin-driven takedown/clear, but derives `active`/`status` from the account's full
`AccountLifecycle` after the write rather than assuming its own dimension won — clearing a
takedown on a still-suspended account must report `suspended`, not `active`. The `#account` frame
shares the same sequencer so account frames are ordered relative to commits.

**Durability and atomicity.** `Firehose::emit_commit`/`emit_account`/`emit_identity`/`emit_sync`
persist each event to
`repo_seq` (via `db::firehose_seq`) **before** broadcasting it, all under one async `emit_lock`
that keeps broadcast order = `seq` order and the log a dense prefix (a failed insert doesn't
consume a `seq`). The sequencer loads `MAX(seq)` on construction, so `seq` is monotonic across
restarts/redeploys. Those methods remain bare best-effort primitives — used directly by tests,
`emit_identity`'s neighbours (`create_handle.rs`/`delete_handle.rs`/`update_handle.rs`), and
`create_did.rs`'s post-commit `emit_account` call, none of which need atomicity with a specific
transaction; the call sites that do instead acquire `emit_lock` via `Firehose::lock_emit`
(returning an `EmitGuard`) *before* opening their transaction, then call
`EmitGuard::stage_commit`/`stage_account` to insert the `repo_seq` row into that *caller's own*
open transaction. A caller that also needs a chained `#sync` in the same transaction (genesis,
activation) calls `PendingCommit::stage_sync`/`PendingAccount::stage_sync`, which inserts the
`#sync` row at the next `seq` and returns a `PendingWithSync` whose `finish` broadcasts the primary
event then the `#sync`, advancing the counter past both. The staging insert lands in the caller's
open transaction — the same one carrying the repo-root CAS (`record_write::commit_repo_write`,
`create_did.rs`'s genesis promotion) or the account-status UPDATE (`activate_account`/
`deactivate_account`) — and get back a `Pending*` handle that carries the guard forward. Acquiring
the lock before the transaction (rather than inside the staging call) matters on this crate's
single-connection pool: `emit_commit`/
`emit_account`/`emit_identity` already acquire the lock before touching the pool, so a staging
path that instead opened its transaction first and acquired the lock after could deadlock against
one of them (each would hold what the other is waiting for). The caller commits that transaction
and only then calls `Pending*::finish` to advance `last_seq` and broadcast; a failed insert rolls
the whole transaction back (via `?`/`Drop`) rather than landing the state change with a
silently-dropped event, and dropping a `Pending*` without finishing never advances the sequence,
so the seq is retried by the next emit. The one asymmetric drop — a handler future cancelled
(client disconnect) *after* its `tx.commit()` made the staged row durable but before `finish` —
leaves `last_seq` behind the durable log; every insert goes through
`Firehose::insert_at_frontier`, which detects the resulting PRIMARY KEY collision, re-derives the
frontier from the durable `MAX(seq)`, and retries once, so one cancelled request costs one
never-broadcast event (still replayable from the log, like any pre-restart event) instead of
wedging all writes until restart. `subscribe_from(cursor)` snapshots the live receiver and
the sequence frontier `upper` together under
`emit_lock`; the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler then pages the durable log for `(cursor, upper]`
(`events_in_range`, decoded via `decode_stored_event`) and streams live events (`seq > upper`)
after — the two ranges are exactly disjoint, so the replay→live boundary has no gap and no
duplication, and replay now survives a restart (it reads the log, not an in-memory buffer). The
subscriber-facing WebSocket frame encoding lives in the `sync_subscribe_repos` handler.

### `crawler.rs`

Outbound `com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl` notifier. `AppState.crawlers: Arc<CrawlerNotifier>`
is shared by every handler. The re-invitation fires from three places: **(1)** on startup
(`main.rs` calls `crawlers.notify()` once when crawlers are configured — a fresh deploy is exactly
when a dropped relay subscription must be re-invited); **(2)** on **every firehose emission**, via
`Firehose::broadcast` (the single fan-out choke point), which the notifier is attached to at boot
(`attach_crawlers`) — so `#commit` **and** the `#account`/`#identity`/`#sync` lifecycle frames all
re-invite the relay, not just repo commits; **(3)** the same broadcast path covers `create_did.rs`/
`create_account_xrpc.rs`/`agent_child.rs`, which additionally call `notify()` directly after their
own commit path. `notify` is fire-and-forget: it selects the crawlers outside their rate-limit
window (one notification per crawler per 30s), then spawns a detached task per crawler that POSTs
`{ "hostname": <PDS-host> }` to `<url>/xrpc/com.atproto.sync.requestCrawl`, retrying with
exponential backoff up to 3 times. All outcomes are logged, never propagated — an emission never
blocks on or fails because of a crawler. Configured via `[crawlers] urls = [...]` (default
`["https://bsky.network"]`; empty disables) or `EZPDS_CRAWLERS`.

Why notify on non-commit frames matters: a relay can silently drop its subscription to a quiet
PDS, and if the PDS only re-invited on commits, a post-migration `#account`(active)/`#sync` burst
emitted while nobody was listening would leave the network's last word on the DID as the source
PDS's deactivation — the DID stuck `AccountDeactivated` network-wide until a repo write happens to
fire another `requestCrawl`. Emitting on the lifecycle frames closes that gap; the durable
`repo_seq` log means the relay's replay heals everything once it reconnects (within retention).

### `relay_status.rs`

The **inbound** half of federation health, complementing `crawler.rs`'s outbound `requestCrawl`:
a `com.atproto.sync.getHostStatus` client that asks the configured relay what it knows about this
PDS. Backs `GET /v1/admin/relay-status` (route `admin_relay_status.rs`), the operator's "is my
server actually federating right now" readout. `fetch_host_status` returns a `RelayReport`:
`Found(HostStatus{ seq, account_count, status })` (the relay's cursor into *our* firehose seq-space,
how many of our accounts it has indexed, and the lifecycle status it assigns us), `NotFound` (the
relay is up but has never crawled us — a normal "not federating yet" state, distinct from an
outage), or `Unreachable(reason)` (transport failure, timeout, non-2xx, or unparseable body). It is
**total, never fatal** — every failure path becomes a variant rather than an `Err`, so the admin
readout always renders the literal truth of what the relay said.

The gap the readout reports is `pdsHeadSeq − relaySeq`, and `pdsHeadSeq` is our **exact** sequencer
head (`firehose.current_seq()`): because we own the PDS, the route reads the head directly instead
of the timed-`subscribeRepos` approximation a third-party observer must make. This module only
fetches the relay's side; `admin_relay_status.rs` does the compare. Like `admin_health.rs`, the
route reports raw truth only — the ok/warn/behind verdict (gap thresholds, status mapping) lives
with the operator (the companion app's relay-status block), never in the API shape. The `#[serde]`
status string is kept verbatim (not an enum) so an unknown value from a newer relay is passed
through rather than dropped. `POST /v1/admin/request-crawl` (route `admin_request_crawl.rs`) is the
companion action: the operator "Request crawl" button, driving `CrawlerNotifier::request_crawl_now`
to re-invite every configured relay immediately (bypassing the 30s auto-notify window) and reporting
each relay's outcome.

### `rate_limit.rs`

Reference-parity request rate limiting. The pure sliding-window algorithm (`MultiWindowLimiter`,
supporting several windows per key with weighted "points") lives in `auth/rate_limit.rs` (Functional
Core); this module is the Imperative Shell that owns the process-level `Mutex`-wrapped limiters and
the Axum middleware. Three families, all off when `[rate_limit] enabled = false` (the test harness
sets this):

1. **Global per-IP** — 1 point/request keyed by client IP (leftmost `X-Forwarded-For`, else the TCP
   peer), default 3000/5min. `com.atproto.sync.getRepo`, `subscribeRepos`, and `_health` are exempt
   so relay backfill/firehose and platform health checks are never throttled.
2. **Per-endpoint per-IP** — tighter caps on `createAccount`/`createSession` (password and
   sovereign session creation share one budget)/`resetPassword`/
   `updateHandle` (plus the native `/v1/accounts[/mobile]` signup routes), `/v1/transfer/accept`
   (authenticated by a bare 6-char code, so a short-code endpoint belongs here by default), and
   the agent claim-ceremony pair `/agent/identity/claim/confirm` + `/v1/agents/claim-preview`
   (both validate a guessable 6-digit `user_code`; they **share one limiter instance** so
   alternating endpoints can't double the guess budget), and the escrow-recovery pair
   `/v1/recovery/initiate` + `/v1/recovery/release` (the release endpoint validates an emailed
   OTP; both **share one limiter instance** so alternating can't double the OTP-guess budget),
   keyed by IP.
3. **Per-account write points** — create=3/update=2/delete=1 over an hourly + daily window, charged
   in `record_write::commit_repo_write` (the single choke point for all four repo-write routes),
   keyed by the **authenticated** DID. Keying on the verified DID — not an unverified token subject —
   is deliberate: otherwise anyone could drain a victim's budget.

Rejections return `429` with the standard error envelope plus `RateLimit-Limit`/`-Remaining`/
`-Reset` and `Retry-After`; successful requests carry the `RateLimit-*` headers of the tightest
applicable limiter. All knobs are configurable via `[rate_limit]` in `pds.toml` / `EZPDS_RATE_LIMIT_*`
(a knob of `0` disables that specific limiter).

### `iroh_tunnel.rs`

The Iroh QUIC tunnel — a NAT-traversing endpoint devices dial by node id instead of by a
routable address. Opt-in via `[iroh] enabled` (default off); when enabled, `main.rs` loads the
persistent node identity (`auth::load_or_create_iroh_secret_key`, backed by the `iroh_identity`
table so the node id is stable across restarts), binds the endpoint with the `N0` preset (n0
discovery + relays), and spawns a detached accept loop. `[iroh] ipv6` (default true;
`EZPDS_IROH_IPV6`) gates the IPv6 QUIC socket: on a v4-only host (e.g. a Railway container with
no public v6 egress) set it false, and `start` clears the pre-configured IP transports and
re-binds IPv4 only — without it iroh's v6 relay probes fail `NetworkUnreachable` forever, one
WARN every ~80s that buries real errors. `AppState.iroh: Option<Arc<IrohState>>`
holds the bound endpoint and its node-id string; `get_device_pds` advertises that node id.
The accept loop speaks a minimal v0.1 echo protocol on the `ezpds/iroh/0` ALPN — enough to
prove the bidirectional channel and serve as a liveness probe; the real repo-sync / push
protocols register here later. Errors are logged, never propagated (one bad peer never stops
the loop). The endpoint is closed on graceful shutdown, which ends the accept loop.

### `read_after_write/`

**Read-after-write:** Buffered munge path for six munged AppView NSIDs
(`app.bsky.feed.getTimeline`, `getAuthorFeed`, `getPostThread`, `getActorLikes`,
`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, `getProfiles`). Merges the requester's unindexed records
(fetched from the firehose event log via `get_records_since_rev`) into the AppView's indexed
response. Selects records by comparing the AppView's `atproto-repo-rev` header to the account's
current repo CID (`repo_seq`): records with `indexed_at` timestamps *after* the AppView's rev
are included. The core `pipethrough_munged` handler implements the full fallback ladder:
(1) upstream error → return error unchanged; (2) non-2xx → return buffered original (except
`getPostThread` 400 NotFound, which triggers reconstruction); (3) JSON parse error → return buffered
original; (4) empty LocalRecords → return buffered original with NO lag header; (5) munge/hydration
errors → log and return buffered original (fallback to untouched upstream response). Response buffering
is capped at 10 MiB; oversized responses trigger early bailout. The `Atproto-Upstream-Lag` header
(milliseconds since the oldest merged record's indexed_at) is set only when local.count > 0.
Submodules:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `mod.rs` | `pipethrough_munged` handler, fallback ladder, buffering cap, response error handling, lag header calculation |
| `munge.rs` | Per-NSID munges `get_timeline`, `get_author_feed`, `get_post_thread`, `get_actor_likes`, `get_profile`, `get_profiles` — injection/overwriting of the requester's records. `// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` (the feed/thread munges orchestrate async hydration through `LocalViewer`) |
| `viewer.rs` | `LocalViewer`: hydrates local records as feed items / profile views with author/counts populated via AppView prefetch, renders quote embeds with appview-fetched URIs (falls back to `#viewNotFound` on errors) |
| `types.rs` | `LocalRecords`, `RecordDescript` — structured container for unindexed records bucket by collection |

The munge path shares `service_proxy::proxy_request` extraction with the streaming fast path
(both mint service auth, both buffer request bodies up to MAX_PROXY_BODY, both forward query params,
both forward the same request/response header subsets — see `service_proxy.rs`'s
`REQ_HEADERS_TO_FORWARD`/`forward_response_headers`).
`mint_service_auth` is `pub(crate)` so `pipethrough_munged` can re-use the JWT minting logic.
Every rung of the fallback ladder returns through the module's `passthrough_response` helper, so a
degraded response still carries the upstream's `atproto-content-labelers`/`atproto-repo-rev`.

**Config:** The AppView is configured via `[appview]` in `pds.toml` (`EZPDS_APPVIEW_URL` env var,
default `https://api.bsky.app`) and `EZPDS_APPVIEW_DID` (default `did:web:api.bsky.app#bsky_appview`).
The optional `EZPDS_APPVIEW_CDN_URL` (default `https://cdn.bsky.app`) overrides the blob CDN
endpoint in blob embed URLs (useful for egress-heavy testing with a local blobstore).

A per-URL refetch cooldown (`[agent_auth] jwks_refetch_cooldown_secs`, stamped per fetch *attempt*) bounds how often the public agent-auth endpoints can force an outbound fetch via an unverified bogus `kid` (or a failing issuer) |

### `routes/`

One file per HTTP endpoint. Each handler is a thin Imperative Shell:
**gather** (extract state/body/headers) → **process** (call `auth/` or `db/`) → **respond**.

| File | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| `oauth_authorize.rs` | `GET/POST /oauth/authorize` |
| `oauth_par.rs` | `POST /oauth/par` — for discoverable (https URL) client_ids, a private-use-scheme redirect_uri must be the client_id host's reverse-FQDN (`invalid_redirect_uri` otherwise), matching bsky.social's enforcement of the atproto OAuth rule |
| `oauth_token/` | `POST /oauth/token` — one route module split across per-grant submodules: `mod.rs` (request/response types, the shared token-issuance + `cleanup_expired_state` helpers, and the `post_token` grant dispatcher) plus `authorization_code.rs`, `refresh.rs`, `jwt_bearer.rs`, and `claim_polling.rs` (each grant's distinct logic + error surface, and its tests). Still a single route module, so the no-routes-importing-routes rule is untouched. Grants: `authorization_code` + `refresh_token` (DPoP-bound, rotating refresh tokens), `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer` (RFC 7523), and `urn:workos:agent-auth:grant-type:claim` (auth.md Step 4c). **jwt-bearer** exchanges a service-signed agent `identity_assertion` for a short-lived **Bearer** access token (no DPoP, no refresh token; the agent identity must be `claimed` with a DID matching the assertion `sub` — unclaimed/absent → `invalid_grant`, `revoked` → `access_denied`, non-origin `resource` → `invalid_target`). The issued token carries the assertion's granular `scope` verbatim (no widening: the grant accepts no requested `scope`) **and** its `registration_id` claim, which marks the token agent-derived (see `auth/extractors.rs::AuthenticatedUser::{is_agent,require_not_agent}`) and ties it to the `agent_identities` row for revocation/audit. **Revocation is bounded by the access-token TTL:** flipping an identity to `revoked` blocks the *next* exchange immediately, but an already-issued access token stays valid until it expires (5 min); there is no live-token revocation list. **claim-polling** is the machine-pollable half of the claim ceremony: a `service_auth`/`anonymous` agent polls with its one-time `claim_token` (no DPoP — it may hold no key yet; the token is the credential) while the owner confirms out-of-band. Reads the identity's lifecycle state and reports it as OAuth device-flow codes — `authorization_pending` (active, ceremony still pending), `expired_token` (`claim_token`/`user_code` window lapsed), `access_denied` (`revoked`), or **200** with a fresh Bearer token + the stored post-claim `identity_assertion` (+ `assertion_expires`) once `claimed` (scope derived from the row's stored scopes, so it matches a jwt-bearer exchange of the same assertion byte-for-byte). Polling faster than the advertised `interval` (`auth/agent_assertion.rs::POLL_INTERVAL_SECS`, 5s) → `slow_down`, throttled by the in-memory `AppState.poll_tracker` keyed by the `claim_token`'s SHA-256 (never the raw secret; pruned in `cleanup_expired_state`) |

Revokes the stateful **refresh token** (`oauth_tokens`); access tokens are self-contained 5-min ES256 JWTs with no server-side store, so an access-token (or any unknown/expired) `token` is accepted as a no-op — its lifetime is already TTL-bounded (same property the `oauth_token/jwt_bearer.rs` note calls out). Auth is DPoP proof-of-possession like the `refresh_token` grant: the proof's key thumbprint must match the token's bound `jkt` (and, when the caller names a `client_id`, its owning client), so a party that only observed the token string can't revoke it — closing the RFC 7009 DoS-oracle concern. Every well-formed, DPoP-authenticated request returns **200 with an empty body** regardless of whether a token matched (RFC 7009 §2.2 non-disclosure); only a missing `token` (`invalid_request`) or a missing/invalid DPoP proof (`invalid_dpop_proof`/`use_dpop_nonce`) returns the `{error, error_description}` shape. | `atproto_did.rs` | `GET /.well-known/atproto-did` |

Host-keyed exactly like `atproto_did.rs`; the opt-in gate is in `db::dids::serve_hosted_did_document`, so a not-opted-in host 404s like an unknown one. One host is the exception, checked *before* the account gate: when the request host maps to the server's own DID (`config.resolve_server_did()` — the same DID `describeServer` advertises), the response is a service-only document synthesized from config (`@context`, `id`, and an `#atproto_pds` service pointing at `public_url`; no verification methods, since inter-service auth is always verified against per-account `#atproto` keys), so the server identity keeps resolving across a public-URL migration with no accounts row. Ordering the config branch first means a coincidental account bearing the server DID can never shadow it; a non-`did:web` `server_did` never matches (`host → did:web:{host}` only produces did:web DIDs), so it falls through to the account path. Serving is deliberately opt-in per account (moving hosting onto Custos removes the independence a standalone host gave the identity) and only ever for user-owned domains — exit is a DNS repoint away |

The document path is the deliberately **non-PLC** doc mutation: it overwrites the stored `did_documents` row (`rewrite_did_document`, requires hosting enabled + `id` matching the DID) and emits an `#identity` firehose frame so relays re-resolve — the `updateHandle`/`refreshIdentity` propagation, no plc.directory round trip. ## Metrics

The federation-health instrument set served by `GET /metrics`. Names and label keys are
constants in `metrics::names` — **this table mirrors that module; change them together.**
Counters are constructed *without* the `_total` suffix (the Prometheus exporter appends it;
a unit test in `metrics.rs` pins the rendered names). All instruments record through the
typed `AppState.metrics` handle; when `[telemetry] metrics_enabled = false` the same handle
drops measurements at the SDK boundary, so call sites never branch.

| Rendered name | Type | Labels | Recorded by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | `route` (matched template or `unmatched`), `status_class` | `metrics::http_metrics_middleware` (outside the rate limiter → 429s count; inside CORS → preflights don't) |
| `firehose_subscribers` | gauge | — | `SubscriberGuard` in `sync_subscribe_repos.rs` (+1 connect, −1 on any exit path) |
| `firehose_events_total` | counter | `frame` (`commit`/`account`/`identity`/`sync`) | `Firehose::broadcast` — the single fan-out choke point |
| `firehose_backfill_window_seconds` | gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each sweep (age of `MIN(sequenced_at)`; 0 when the log is empty) |
| `firehose_gc_swept_total` / `firehose_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `firehose_gc.rs` after each completed pass |
| `labeler_watch_changes_total` / `labeler_watch_last_run_timestamp` | counter / gauge | — | `labeler_watch.rs` after each completed pass (`changes` = label rows upserted + removed; error early-returns skip the timestamp on purpose — staleness is the alarm) |
| `blob_gc_swept_total` / `blob_gc_errors_total` / `blob_gc_last_run_timestamp` | counter / counter / gauge | — | `blob_gc.rs` after each completed pass (a failed-to-start pass leaves the timestamp stale on purpose — that staleness is the alarm). `errors` counts **failures**, of two kinds sharing one counter because both mean "the pass left work undone": one per account whose reconcile errored, and one per expired ownership row the sweep failed to delete. A failed account is excluded from the sweep entirely (fail closed — its references could not be computed, so its blobs must not be collected) and leaks disk until the fault is fixed. Note it contributes exactly **1** regardless of how many blobs go uncollected — the account that motivated this counter reports `1` while leaving 534 blobs behind; the per-account blob count is the `blobs_skipped` log field, not this metric. ## Hard Rules

**Routes must not import from other routes.**
If two routes share logic, that logic belongs in `auth/` (pure) or `db/` (queries). A route
importing from another route creates hidden coupling and makes it impossible to reason about
a handler in isolation.

**Every `.rs` file with runtime behavior must have a pattern comment.**
Add `// pattern: Functional Core`, `// pattern: Imperative Shell`, or
`// pattern: Mixed (unavoidable)` at the top of any file containing functions or
orchestration logic. Files with only types, constants, or re-exports are exempt.

**`db/` submodules own queries, not transactions.**
Business-logic transactions (multi-table atomic operations) live in the route handler or
a dedicated helper called by the handler — not inside `db/` functions. `db/` functions
accept `&SqlitePool` or `&mut SqliteTransaction`; they never open transactions themselves
unless the operation is inherently single-table.

**Authentication must never be cookie-based; permissive CORS on the public surface depends on it.**
`app.rs` applies `CorsLayer::permissive()` to the public surface (landing, `.well-known`, OAuth,
agent registration, all XRPC, static assets) but deliberately **not** to the admin/provisioning
`/v1/*` surface (same-origin only). Permissive CORS is safe only because every auth path is
Bearer/DPoP/signed-request — never an ambient cookie — so a hostile origin cannot ride a logged-in
user's credentials. If any future auth mechanism becomes cookie-based, the permissive CORS layer
must be tightened (explicit origin allowlist + credentials handling) in the same change.

## Adding a New Route

1. Create `src/routes/<name>.rs` with `// pattern: Imperative Shell` at the top.
2. If the handler needs shared auth logic → add to `auth/` (pure) or use an existing extractor.
3. If the handler needs a new DB query → add to the appropriate `db/` submodule.
4. If it's an XRPC procedure: a JSON input body is parsed with `LexiconInput<T>` (never bare
   `axum::Json<T>`) after vendoring its lexicon document (`crates/pds/lexicons/README.md`); a
   no-input procedure takes `NoInputBody` instead. Both must be the handler's final extractor.
5. Register in `src/app.rs` router.
6. Add a `.bru` file in `bruno/` (see root AGENTS.md).

## Adding a New DB Query

content.thinking:
I'm thinking through the architecture here: the `NotifyQueue` struct will wrap both the sender and an atomic counter for tracking queue depth. When jobs are sent, the counter increments; when the worker processes them, it decrements. This gives us a push-based metric for the gauge while keeping the health endpoint able to pull the current depth on demand.

There's a key decision about *when* to decrement — right after receiving the job from the queue, or after it finishes running. The difference matters: decrementing at receive shows jobs waiting, while decrementing after completion shows outstanding work including in-flight jobs. During relay outages where jobs can hang for 30+ seconds, tracking the in-flight job as part of the depth is more meaningful, so I'm leaning toward decrementing after the job completes.

I'm torn on whether to ask the user about this semantic choice or just implement it with a clear, easy-to-flip seam and invite them to adjust. Since the session isn't interactive and the instruction says to make routine judgment calls myself, I'll go ahead with the "outstanding including in-flight" approach and mark the decision point clearly for them.

Now I'm setting up the metrics instrumentation—I need a gauge to track queue depth as a u64 counter, and I'm restructuring NotifySender to hold both the channel sender and an atomic counter wrapped in an Arc so the depth can be updated and read by the metrics system.

The tricky part is handling the increment-before-send pattern safely: if the send fails because the worker is gone, I need to decrement the counter back to avoid a false depth reading. I'm also checking whether to use AtomicI64 or AtomicU64—AtomicI64 would make underflows visible as a defensive measure, though with correct pairing it shouldn't happen.

content.text:
Now I have the shape of the problem. Two things drive the design:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `tokio::sync::mpsc::UnboundedReceiver` does have `len()`, but the receiver is *moved into* the worker task — so nothing outside it can sample the depth. The health endpoint's pull-read requirement is what forces a shared counter rather than a `len()` sample.
- `metrics.rs` gauges are **write-only in-process** (only a Prometheus scrape observes them), which is exactly why `sweep_status.rs` exists as a parallel readable mirror. The same split applies here: an OTel gauge for scraping, a shared atomic for `/v1/admin/health`.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Metrics is currently built *after* the notify worker in `main.rs`, so that ordering has to flip.

content.content:
Custos can now send push notifications, and the first one is live: when an agent asks to act on your behalf, your phone tells you instead of the request waiting silently until you next open the app. Point your instance at a relay with `[notifications] relay` and the feature switches on; leave it unset and none of it exists — no keys are generated, no registration endpoints answer, nothing is sent. Notifications are sealed on your instance to one specific device and opened only on that device, so neither the relay nor Apple ever sees what a notification says. They also prove where they came from: your instance signs each one with a key your devices have pinned, so a relay that turned hostile could drop or repeat notifications but could never write one that looks genuine. Length is padded to fixed sizes, because how long a notification is would otherwise reveal what kind it is; anything too large to pad is dropped rather than sent in a way that leaks. Devices register over the app's normal authenticated channel and can unregister at any time, and when Apple reports a device is gone, its registration is removed at once. Deleting an account or revoking an operator device also tells the relay to forget the devices involved. Operators rotate the signing keys with `pds notification-keys` — publish a new key alongside the old, retire the old once devices have re-pinned, or revoke it outright if it is compromised.
----

input.content: Operators can now see how much push-notification work is waiting. The notification queue holds jobs in memory and never blocks a request, which is the right trade when a relay is slow — but it also meant that a relay being down for a maintenance window, or pointed at the wrong node id, showed up only as a rising count of warnings in the log. There is now a `notify_queue_depth` metric alongside the others at `/metrics`, and a `notifyQueueDepth` figure in the operator health readout that the console can show. It counts the jobs still outstanding, including the one currently being attempted, so a single push stuck against an unreachable relay is visible rather than reading as an empty queue. Expect zero; a number that climbs and stays there is a relay outage becoming a memory cost. Instances with no relay configured report nothing at all rather than a misleading zero.

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
Notify: expose the send worker's queue depth as a metric (MM-487)

The notification send worker drains an unbounded mpsc with a single
sequential task — the right trade for a best-effort, device-count-scaled
feature, since the queue must never block a request path. But during a
prolonged relay outage the queue grows without bound in the interim, and
that was only inferable from `warn!` volume.

Add a `notify_queue_depth` gauge and mirror it as `notifyQueueDepth` on
`GET /v1/admin/health`, so the Brass Console can show it. The health
readout reads a shared atomic rather than the gauge (OTel instruments are
write-only in-process, the same reason `sweep_status.rs` exists), so it
works with `[telemetry] metrics_enabled` off, and reports `null` rather
than `0` when no relay is configured.

The counter is decremented after a job finishes rather than at `recv`, so
the depth counts outstanding work rather than only what is waiting: during
the outage this metric exists for, each job burns the full 30s stream
timeout, and a single stuck job is real backlog that a depth of 0 would
misreport.

Two incidental consequences:

- `NotifySender` becomes a struct (the receiver is moved into the worker
  task, so its `len()` is unreachable from the health route). Its `send`
  is now infallible and logs the stopped-worker case itself — every one
  of the five call sites discarded that `Result` identically, and clippy
  refuses the large `Err` variant on a local function.
- The metrics pipeline is built before the notify worker in `main.rs`,
  since the worker now records through it.

This metric is the prerequisite for deciding, with evidence, whether the
queue should stay unbounded or gain a drop-oldest cap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && gh pr create --base main --title "Notify: expose the send worker's queue depth as a metric (MM-487)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Closes MM-487. Follow-up from review on #467 (MM-418).

## What

The notification send worker drains an **unbounded** `tokio::sync::mpsc` with a single sequential task. That is the right trade-off for a best-effort, device-count-scaled feature — the queue must never block a request path, and a missed push is a missed banner rather than lost data. But during a prolonged relay outage (a maintenance window, a misconfigured node id) the queue grows without bound in the interim, and that was only inferable from `warn!` volume.

- **`notify_queue_depth`** gauge + its `metrics::names` constant, recorded on both edges of the queue.
- **`notifyQueueDepth`** on `GET /v1/admin/health`, so the Brass Console can show it. It reads a shared atomic rather than the gauge — OTel instruments are write-only in-process, which is the same reason `sweep_status.rs` mirrors its gauges — so it works with `[telemetry] metrics_enabled` off. `null` when no relay is configured, which is a different fact from an empty queue.
- The row in `crates/pds/AGENTS.md`'s metrics table, which mirrors `metrics::names`.

## Decisions worth a reviewer's attention

**Decremented after the job runs, not at `recv`.** The depth counts outstanding work including the one in flight, rather than only what is waiting. During the outage this metric exists for, each job burns the full 30s stream timeout — a single stuck job is real backlog, and a depth that read 0 through it would be reporting the wrong thing.

**A shared atomic rather than `UnboundedReceiver::len()`.** The receiver is moved into the worker task, so nothing outside it can sample the depth; the health endpoint's pull-read is what forces the counter.

**The counter lives in a `QueueDepth` held separately from the sender.** A `NotifySender` clone inside the worker task would keep `tx` alive, so `rx.recv()` could never report the queue closed.

## Incidental consequences

- `NotifySender` goes from a type alias to a struct. Its `send` is now **infallible** and logs the stopped-worker case itself: all five call sites discarded that `Result` identically with `let _ =`, and clippy's `result_large_err` refuses the large `Err` variant on a local function. A dropped job is now logged once instead of silently swallowed in five places.
- The metrics pipeline is built before the notify worker in `main.rs`, since the worker now records through it.

## Open question, unchanged

Whether the queue should stay unbounded now that it is observable, or gain a cap that drops oldest-first. Dropping is consistent with the feature's best-effort posture; this metric is the prerequisite for deciding with evidence either way. Not decided here.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p pds` — 2279 + 1 pass, including the notify loopback e2e.
- `cargo clippy -p pds --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt -p pds --check` clean.
- `just ticket-ref-check` / `changelog-check` / `bruno-check` / `docs-check` / `capability-docs-check` green.
- New tests: depth counts enqueued jobs and is shared across clones; a send to a stopped worker does not inflate it; the worker returns the depth to zero as it drains **even when every job fails** (the outage case). The metrics test pins `notify_queue_depth` rendering as a gauge, not a counter.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

content.text:
PR is open: [malpercio-dev/ezpds#471](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/471).

**One thing I couldn't do:** move MM-487 to "In Review" and attach the PR link. The Linear MCP server (`plugin:linear:linear`) needs OAuth and this session is non-interactive, so the write path is unavailable — you'll need to authorize it via your claude.ai connector settings (or `/mcp` in an interactive session) and then transition it, or flip it by hand.

## What landed

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| `notify_queue_depth` gauge + name constant | [metrics.rs](crates/pds/src/metrics.rs) |
| `NotifySender` struct + `QueueDepth` counter | [notify_relay_client.rs](crates/pds/src/notify_relay_client.rs) |
| `notifyQueueDepth` in the health readout | [admin_health.rs:45](crates/pds/src/routes/admin_health.rs:45) |
| Metrics table row | [crates/pds/AGENTS.md](crates/pds/AGENTS.md) |

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- **Ownership decided the shape.** The obvious `rx.len()` is unreachable — the receiver is *moved into* the worker task. And the first fix I wrote (worker holds a `NotifySender` clone) would have kept `tx` alive inside the task, meaning `rx.recv()` could never return `None` and the "queue closed" shutdown path would be dead code. Splitting the counter into its own `QueueDepth` is what lets the worker decrement without owning a sender.
- **Clippy forced a better API.** `result_large_err` rejected `Result<(), SendError<NotifyJob>>` because `NotifyJob::Push` carries several `String`s. Since all five call sites already wrote `let _ = sender.send(...)`, making `send` infallible and logging inside it turned a lint into a real improvement — a dropped job now produces one `warn!` instead of vanishing silently in five places.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## The decision I made on your behalf

The depth decrements **after** each job finishes, not at `recv` — so it counts outstanding work including the in-flight job, not just what's queued behind it. My reasoning: during a relay outage each job burns the full 30s `STREAM_TIMEOUT`, so one stuck job is genuine backlog that a `recv`-time decrement would report as an empty queue. That's a one-line flip in `spawn_worker` if you'd rather it mean "waiting only" — say the word and I'll change it along with the doc table.

The issue's open question (unbounded vs. drop-oldest cap) I deliberately left open — this metric is the evidence-gathering step for it, and capping now would be deciding it blind.

Verification: full `cargo test -p pds` (2279 + 1 passing, including the notify loopback e2e), clippy `-D warnings`, fmt, and the five relevant `just` doc/parity gates all green.
